question: Should OpenClaw accept this restart-specific durable shared-SQLite audit table now, with its fixed retention and redacted metadata boundary, or wait for a broader audit-ledger design?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a concrete code defect; it is whether the new persisted metadata surface is the desired product/security boundary for restart forensics.

options.title: Accept after refresh
options.body: Resolve the current-main conflicts, keep the 512-row redacted restart audit table, and merge once maintainers accept the storage/privacy contract.

options.title: Narrow stored metadata first
options.body: Require a smaller column/payload set or stricter redaction policy before accepting durable restart audit storage.

options.title: Pause for broader audit ledger
options.body: Close or pause this PR if restart records should wait for the broader metadata audit-ledger direction instead of landing as a separate producer now.

recommendation.title: Accept after refresh
recommendation.body: Resolve the current-main conflicts, keep the 512-row redacted restart audit table, and merge once maintainers accept the storage/privacy contract.

likelyOwner.reason: His history spans both restart deferral/tracing and the shared SQLite state database, making him the best available owner for this storage-boundary choice.
